questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best exercises for losing weight quickly
How to train properly for a half marathon
Why eating sugar is bad for your health
How new weight loss drugs work and affect people
questions.why: They discuss drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro, how they work, and one user's experience.

questions.q: What does Neil say about his own efforts to stay healthy?
options: He has stopped exercising because of an injury
He exercises and eats well, but isn't sure it works
He is taking weight loss drugs from his doctor
He is training hard for his first marathon
questions.why: He follows an exercise routine and eats healthily, but isn't sure it's having much effect.

questions.q: What does Georgie say about her lifestyle?
options: She runs a lot but still eats lots of sugar
She only eats salad and drinks water
She never does any exercise because she's busy
She has given up sugar completely this year
questions.why: She's training for a half marathon, 'but I still eat a lot of sugar'.

questions.q: Roughly how many British adults are estimated to be overweight?
options: About 20%
About 40%
About 65%
About 90%
questions.why: Neil says around 65% of British adults are estimated to be overweight.

questions.q: How do weight loss drugs like Ozempic work?
options: They speed up how fast your body burns energy
They copy hormones that make you feel full
They stop the body from absorbing any sugar
They make all food taste bad, so you eat less
questions.why: Georgie says they're modified natural hormones that make us feel full, and the effect lasts longer.

questions.q: What happened when Lynne Massey-Davis used Mounjaro?
options: She felt hungry all the time
She stopped after one month
She gained weight at first
She lost 20kg in six months
questions.why: Georgie says Lynne lost 20kg in six months using Mounjaro.

questions.q: Why does Lynne talk about an angel and a devil on her shoulders?
options: To describe a strange dream she had as a child
To explain why she decided to become a doctor
To describe the fight in her mind about food
To joke about the advice her friends give her
questions.why: She uses it to explain 'food noise': one voice said don't eat, the other said have a taste.

questions.q: According to Professor Giles Yeo, how did doctors discover these drugs help weight loss?
options: People taking them for diabetes lost weight as a side effect
They were tested on athletes
Companies designed them for weight loss from the start
Patients asked for them
questions.why: He says Ozempic was first for diabetes, then people noticed, as a side effect, weight loss.
